clips.title: Sarcasm
clips.listenFor: Plain should sound sincere. Directed should mean the opposite of the words. Nothing in the text marks the sarcasm, so only direction can carry it.
clips.text: Thanks for updating the spreadsheet. I can tell you put a lot of care into it.

direction.prose: Dry, cutting sarcasm. The speaker is annoyed and means the opposite of every word. Lean on 'a lot of care'
direction.tagged: [sarcastically] Thanks for updating the spreadsheet. [dryly] I can tell you put a lot of care into it.
direction.voxtral: [emotion=sarcastic]Thanks for updating the spreadsheet. I can tell you put a lot of care into it.

clips.title: Anger held in check
clips.listenFor: Plain: firm, a little annoyed. Directed: quiet, clipped anger, with no shouting.
clips.text: I asked for the report on Monday. It's Thursday. I'm going to need it by the end of today.

direction.prose: Barely contained fury: quiet, clipped, every word deliberate. Do not shout
direction.tagged: [quietly furious] I asked for the report on Monday. [coldly] It's Thursday. [through gritted teeth] I'm going to need it by the end of today.
direction.grok: <slow>I asked for the report on Monday.</slow> [pause] <soft>It's Thursday.</soft> [pause] <slow>I'm going to need it by the end of today.</slow>
direction.voxtral: [emotion=tense][pace=slow]I asked for the report on Monday. [emotion=critical]It's Thursday. [emotion=tense]I'm going to need it by the end of today.

clips.title: Staying late
clips.listenFor: Plain should sound willing. Directed should still agree, but you should hear that the speaker would rather not.
clips.text: Sure, I can stay late tonight.

direction.prose: Agreeing, but tired and a little put-upon: you'll do it, and you'd rather not.
direction.tagged: [sighs] [reluctantly] Sure, I can stay late tonight.

clips.title: A list in Markdown
clips.listenFor: A pause between items, and the comma inside "two forms of ID, one with a photo" not heard as a new item. Whether the bullets are read aloud.
clips.text:
Before you leave, pack:

- the charger
- the blue folder with the lease
- two forms of ID, one with a photo
- the spare key for the side door

clips.title: Code-switching on look-alike words
clips.listenFor: "son las once" as Spanish and "also gut" as German, though both are spelled like English words.
clips.text: When I asked about the train, she said "son las once," so we'd missed it. My uncle just shrugged: "also gut."
clips.pronounce: son lahs OHN-seh ("it's eleven o'clock"); AHL-zo goot ("well, fine").

direction.prose: Speak in natural American English, but say the quoted Spanish and German phrases in those languages.
direction.tagged: When I asked about the train, she said [in Spanish] "son las once," so we'd missed it. My uncle just shrugged: [in German] "also gut."

clips.title: Dialog
clips.listenFor: The quoted lines set apart from the narration, the question rising, and "You think so?" as a doubtful repeat.
clips.text:
"Did you lock the door?" she asked.

"I think so."

"You think so?" He was already reaching for his keys.

direction.prose: Read it like an audiobook narrator: give the quoted lines a little life, and leave a short pause between lines of dialog.
direction.tagged:
"Did you lock the door?" she asked.

[pause] "I think so."

[pause] "You think so?" He was already reaching for his keys.
direction.grok:
"Did you lock the door?" she asked.

[pause] "I think so."

[pause] "You think so?" He was already reaching for his keys.

clips.title: Worked math
clips.listenFor: "not eight" said as a correction, and stress on the second "then": double first, then add. In the Markdown version, whether the underscores are read aloud.
clips.text: If x is three, then two x plus one is seven, not eight: you double first, then add the one.

variants.label: Markdown _then_
variants.text: If x is three, then two x plus one is seven, not eight: you double first, _then_ add the one.

clips.title: Water boiling
clips.listenFor: The units read as words (degrees Celsius, meters), the aside in parentheses set off, and the contrast between sea level and altitude.
clips.text: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level, but at 3,000 m (about twice the height of Denver) it boils at about 90, which is why pasta takes longer up there.

direction.prose: Explain it like a patient teacher, so the contrast between sea level and altitude is clear.
direction.tagged: [patiently] Water boils at 100 °C at sea level, but at 3,000 m (about twice the height of Denver) it boils at about 90, which is why pasta takes longer up there.
direction.voxtral: [emotion=calm]Water boils at 100 °C at sea level, but at 3,000 m (about twice the height of Denver) it boils at about 90, which is why pasta takes longer up there.

clips.title: Word stress
clips.listenFor: The marked word stressed, and only that one. Stress on "she" means someone else stole it; stress on "money" means she stole something else. Plain is the baseline.
clips.text: I didn't say she stole the money.

direction.prose: Stress the word 'she'; it carries the meaning of the sentence.
Stress the word 'money'; it carries the meaning of the sentence.

variants.label: Markdown *she*
variants.text: I didn't say *she* stole the money.
